title: DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS JOB DESCRIPTION
text:
Reports To: Chief Executive Officer

Directly Supervises: Executive Operations Coordinator, Administrative Manager, Administrative Assistants, Revenue Cycle Manager, Operations Manager, and other operational employees assigned by the Chief Executive Officer

Schedule: Full-time; 40 hours per week, with scheduling flexibility based on operational needs

Compensation: As stated in the signed offer or compensation agreement

Work Arrangement: Primarily remote, with weekly on-site presence required at Elevation's Homewood and Matteson offices

COMPENSATION AND HOURS

* This is a full-time, salaried-exempt position scheduled for 40 hours per week. The employee will receive the salary stated in the signed offer or compensation agreement and is not eligible for overtime compensation.

* If time reporting is required for attendance, workload, leave, or administrative purposes, the employee must accurately record actual hours worked. Time entries do not change the established salary.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Director of Operations ensures that Elevation Individual & Family Therapy's administrative and operational functions are organized, accountable, compliant, and aligned with client-service and financial goals. The position reduces the CEO's involvement in routine operations by resolving matters within the role's authority, ensuring assigned work is completed, and presenting recommendations when executive approval is required.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

1. OPERATIONAL LEADERSHIP AND STAFF ACCOUNTABILITY

* Set priorities, deadlines, performance expectations, and coverage plans for assigned staff across both locations.

* Conduct regular supervision meetings and monitor attendance, responsiveness, accuracy, productivity, professionalism, and follow-through.

* Review required reports and promptly address missed deadlines, repeated errors, unresolved concerns, and incomplete work.

* Provide training, coaching, written expectations, and documented corrective feedback; coordinate performance improvement or disciplinary processes with the Executive Operations Coordinator and CEO.

* Assign each operational concern to an appropriate owner, monitor it through resolution, and escalate only matters requiring executive, legal, financial, clinical, or regulatory authority.

2. ADMINISTRATIVE AND CLIENT-SERVICE OPERATIONS

* Oversee phone and voicemail coverage, new-client inquiries, intake follow-up, insurance verification, required paperwork, scheduling, check-in, and appointment confirmation.

* Monitor re-engagement, no-show and cancellation outreach, copay collection, approved payment-plan workflows, and records requests.

* Ensure administrative staff consistently follow approved scripts, workflows, response-time standards, documentation requirements, and escalation procedures.

* Oversee office calendars, room assignments, supplies, equipment, routine facility concerns, and administrative coverage.

* Coordinate with clinical leadership when an operational concern affects client care, provider scheduling, documentation, or referrals.

3. REVENUE CYCLE OVERSIGHT

* Directly supervise the Revenue Cycle Manager, establish performance expectations, review results, provide coaching and accountability, and ensure timely follow-through on revenue-cycle priorities.

* Hold the Revenue Cycle Manager accountable for routine billing operations and supervision of assigned billing staff; coordinate cross-department priorities and escalate unresolved financial, payer, staffing, or compliance risks to the CEO.

* Review reports related to claims, denials, payment posting, insurance follow-up, patient balances, accounts receivable, and collections.

* Ensure billing concerns are assigned, documented, and resolved within established timelines.

* Identify administrative or clinical workflow failures that contribute to denials, delayed billing, inaccurate balances, or lost revenue.

* Coordinate communication among RCM, administrative, clinical, and collections staff and escalate material payer, financial, or compliance concerns.

4. POLICIES, SOPS, AND EHR WORKFLOW IMPROVEMENT

* Identify processes requiring a written policy, SOP, checklist, script, workflow, quality check, or escalation procedure.

* Draft and update operational policies and SOPs with the employees and subject-matter experts responsible for the work; coordinate approval by the appropriate leader.

* Maintain version control, review dates, distribution, training, employee acknowledgment, and monitoring of approved procedures.

* Evaluate EHR and technology workflows for intake, scheduling, documentation tracking, billing, records, client communication, and reporting.

* Identify duplicate entry, inconsistent data, preventable delays, and unnecessary manual work; recommend and coordinate approved templates, reports, alerts, tracking tools, automations, and vendor requests.

* Test approved changes, document the revised workflow, coordinate staff training, and monitor implementation while protecting confidentiality and system access.

5. HR, CREDENTIALING, AND COMPLIANCE COORDINATION

Directly supervise the Executive Operations Coordinator by establishing priorities, monitoring deadlines and accuracy, reviewing performance, and ensuring timely completion of assigned HR administration, credentialing, compliance, records, onboarding, offboarding, and policy-related responsibilities. The Executive Operations Coordinator or other assigned personnel retain responsibility for completing the detailed administrative work and maintaining required records.

* Ensure employee performance, attendance, conduct, onboarding, offboarding, training, personnel documentation, and policy-acknowledgment processes are coordinated appropriately and escalated to the CEO when executive authority or protected reporting is required.

* Review credentialing, recredentialing, payer enrollment, licensure, renewal, training, and compliance trackers; ensure assigned staff follow up on incomplete or at-risk items.

* Coordinate provider status changes with HR, billing, clinical leadership, scheduling, and provider-directory workflows.

* Monitor completion of corrective actions and escalate material delays, expirations, privacy concerns, payer or government inquiries, suspected fraud, client-safety issues, or other significant risks immediately.

* Support audits, internal reviews, payer requests, and corrective-action plans without acting as Elevation's attorney or sole clinical compliance authority.

6. BUDGET AND EXPENSE MONITORING

* Assist the CEO with preparing and monitoring approved administrative and operational budgets.

* Review actual operational expenses against approved amounts, including administrative and billing staffing costs, overtime, office supplies, software subscriptions, vendor charges, and upcoming renewals.

* Identify unusual spending, recurring overages, duplicate services, avoidable expenses, and practical opportunities for cost savings.

* Coordinate with billing and collections personnel to identify preventable revenue leakage related to denials, delayed claims, workflow errors, missed collections, or unresolved client balances.

* Maintain organized records of approved operational purchases and recurring expenses and submit purchase or budget-adjustment requests with the cost, purpose, priority, and recommendation.

* Provide the CEO with a monthly summary of significant budget variances, anticipated expenses, and recommended corrective or cost-saving actions.

7. REPORTING AND LEADERSHIP COLLABORATION

* Provide a concise weekly CEO report covering accomplishments, unresolved matters, staff concerns, revenue cycle issues, credentialing/compliance risks, budget concerns, and policy, SOP, or EHR project status.

* Provide a monthly operational summary identifying trends, recurring problems, performance patterns, completed improvements, and recommended priorities.

* Present significant concerns with relevant facts, actions already taken, and a recommended solution rather than forwarding unorganized information.

* Directly supervise the Administrative Manager and Administrative Assistants. Establish priorities, monitor performance, and maintain formal accountability while using the Administrative Manager's workflow knowledge and assigned functional ownership to support training, quality, office operations, and consistent administrative processes.

8. GROWTH INITIATIVES AND PROGRAM IMPLEMENTATION

* Lead the operational assessment of CEO-directed growth opportunities, including new services, programs, partnerships, and location expansions. Work with clinical leadership, revenue cycle, and other relevant staff to assess demand, staffing, costs, reimbursement where applicable, space and technology needs, and implementation risks. Clinical leadership guides clinical program design.

* Present the CEO with a recommendation, estimated costs and resources, and a proposed timeline. The CEO decides which opportunities move forward.

* Lead the rollout of approved initiatives. Build the launch plan, assign responsibilities and deadlines, coordinate training and workflow changes, track milestones, and report progress and early results to the CEO.

ROLE BOUNDARIES AND DECISION-MAKING AUTHORITY

The Director of Operations owns operational follow-through but does not personally perform every task within the functions overseen. The position may assign and prioritize routine work, require status updates, provide coaching and corrective feedback, implement approved procedures, coordinate across departments, and resolve routine administrative or client-service concerns within established policies.

CEO approval is required before hiring, termination, suspension, compensation changes, material policy changes, unapproved contracts or purchases, new recurring expenses, significant balance waivers, banking or debt decisions, public statements, or substantive responses to legal, government, payer, or regulatory matters. The Director of Operations monitors and recommends but does not replace bookkeeping, payroll, accounting, or executive financial authority.

SCHEDULE AND CAPACITY

* Periodic on-site presence at both Elevation offices is required to observe day-to-day workflows, the office environment, staff performance, client-service operations, and implementation of policies and procedures. The timing and frequency of visits will be based on operational needs and CEO direction.

* The regular schedule will be established by the CEO and will generally total 40 hours per week. Some evening or weekend work may be necessary based on operational needs. The employee must maintain agreed-upon availability during core business hours for supervision, meetings, and time-sensitive matters.

* Continuous after-hours availability is not expected; after-hours contact should generally be limited to urgent matters that cannot reasonably wait. Occasional schedule fluctuations do not change the position's established salary.

* The Director of Operations must notify the CEO when workload or competing priorities cannot reasonably be completed within the established 40-hour schedule and recommend what should be delegated, postponed, or reprioritized.

* Unless otherwise approved, the role should generally carry no more than two major operational improvement projects at one time. Major launches count toward this limit unless the CEO approves an exception.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

* At least three years of relevant operations, healthcare administration, office management, or employee-supervision experience.

* Demonstrated ability to supervise employees, address performance concerns, analyze operational data, and independently move work to completion.

* Strong judgment, initiative, organization, problem-solving, discretion, emotional maturity, and written and verbal communication skills.

* Ability to draft clear policies, SOPs, reports, checklists, and workflows and to protect confidential client, employee, financial, and business information.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Outlook, spreadsheets, cloud-based systems, and the ability to learn and improve EHR and business platforms.

* Working knowledge of HIPAA and healthcare confidentiality expectations; reliable transportation and ability to work from both Elevation locations as required.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's degree in business, healthcare administration, management, human resources, or a related field; behavioral health or healthcare operations experience; and experience with revenue cycle, credentialing, compliance, EHR workflow improvement, SOP development, reporting, dashboards, or automations.
